findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded during web requests, not for background or console lookups
findings.body: translate() only calls load_locale(config.locale). The fallback chain (default locale and :en) is loaded only by ApplicationController#set_locale via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Outside a web request (background jobs such as Sidekiq email delivery, rake tasks, the console, or a process that has not served a request yet), I18n.locale is e.g. :fr, so only :fr translations are loaded. Fallbacks#translate then asks the Simple backend for :en or default-locale strings that were never loaded, and keys missing from the non-English locale come back as 'translation missing' instead of the English text. That is the exact case this feature is meant to fix. The fallback chain should be loaded from the translate path (for example by loading I18n.fallbacks[config.locale] here), not only from the controller filter.

findings.title: LRU translation cache key ignores the fallback chain it now depends on
findings.body: With fallbacks enabled, the value returned for (key, locale) depends on the fallback chain, which depends on SiteSetting.default_locale and on which fallback locales happen to be loaded at lookup time. The cache key is only key + config.locale + backend object_id, and nothing in this change invalidates entries when default_locale changes or when a fallback locale is loaded later. The first computed value, including a 'translation missing' string that is frozen and cached at line 75, is then served until LRU eviction (300 entries) or reload!.

findings.title: Every I18n lookup now reads SiteSetting and allocates a fallback array
findings.body: Fallbacks#translate, included into the backend at line 9, calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] on every lookup that reaches the backend. That means this method runs for every translation, including calls with interpolation arguments that bypass the LRU cache (translate_accelerator.rb line 69). Each call reads SiteSetting.default_locale and builds and uniq/compacts a new array. I18n previously had no dependency on SiteSetting, so any I18n.t during boot or in tasks where settings are not yet readable (asset precompile, migrations) can now trigger a SiteSetting load and hit the database. Memoizing the chain per (locale, default_locale) would remove both costs.

findings.title: No specs cover the new fallback behavior or the load path
findings.body: This change affects global translation behavior: a new fallback chain, the fallback backend module included globally, pluralization moved from pluralization.rb into this file, config.i18n.fallbacks removed from three environment files, and a new ensure_loaded! path in set_locale and the accelerator. The PR adds no specs. Nothing verifies that a key missing in a non-English locale resolves through the site default and then :en, that the fallback works when the fallback locale has not been loaded (the gap described in translate_accelerator.rb line 68), or that pluralization still works after the include was moved. A unit test for FallbackLocaleList#[] and a request spec exercising set_locale with a missing key would catch these regressions.
